key_evidence: On 2026-09-21 the Abu Dhabi Labour Court was reported to have recovered Dh7.8 million (about $2.1 million) in unpaid wages for 948 workers across three resolved collective disputes, with full payment secured for 457 workers and partial payment for 491 more under structured instalment plans.

Attribution is clean: the Abu Dhabi Labour Court sits within the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, an emirate-level institution. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and the Wage Protection System are federal and are used as context only, not scored as Abu Dhabi’s conduct.

Directionality: Abu Dhabi surfaced on POSITIVE in-window evidence, so screening rule 3 permits upward movement. The positive conduct is specific and enacted (a court moving money to identified workers), not the mere absence of new harm.

THE REASON THIS IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN RECOMMENDED: every positive figure originates with the UAE government or Emirati outlets (The National, which is UAE-owned, Arabian Business, Gulf News). No independent audit or ILO verification of these figures was located. AC1 is therefore held at 3/5 rather than 4/5.

Countervailing evidence holds the low end of the profile: HRW World Report 2026 records that employers retain disproportionate control under the kafala system, that false absconding charges expose workers to detention and deportation, that wage theft, recruitment fees and passport confiscation persist in conditions that may amount to forced labour, that trade unions remain banned, and that there is no non-discriminatory minimum wage. EQU stays at 1.8, BND at 1.6 and INT at 1.6.
Only three dimensions move materially (BND +0.6, ACC +0.7, INT +0.6) and all three move off an absolute floor that asserted nothing works at all. No band change: Developing to Developing.

evidence.quote: Full payments were secured for 457 workers, while 491 others received partial payments, with remaining balances placed under structured instalment plans.
evidence.claim: The Abu Dhabi Labour Court delivered differentiated outcomes calibrated to employer capacity rather than a uniform refusal, supporting AC2 at 3/5 and B4 Refusal Ethics at 3/5 against a published BND floor of 1.0.

evidence.quote: The ministry resolved 185,793 labour disputes amicably in the first half of this year, representing 98.6 per cent of all cases.
evidence.claim: Government-published dispute-resolution data, including the 1.4% residual referred to the judiciary, supports A1 at 4/5 and AB3 at 3/5. Not independently verified.

evidence.quote: Resolved disputes allowed affected workers to retain their jobs, maintaining stable employment and ensuring business continuity for the companies involved.
evidence.claim: Resolution preserved employment as well as recovering wages, supporting AC5 Follow-Through at 3/5.
Abu Dhabi recovered AED 7.81 million (about $2.13 million) for 948 workers across three collective labour cases resolved within three months.

MoHRE settled 185,793 labour disputes amicably in H1 2026 (98.6% of cases), with 2,481 (1.4%) referred to the judiciary, and attributes part of the improvement to Wage Protection System upgrades that identify payment delays at an early stage.

Employers still hold disproportionate control over migrant workers under the kafala sponsorship system; employers can file false absconding charges against workers who leave abusive jobs, risking detention and deportation; wage theft, illegal recruitment fees and passport confiscation persist in conditions that may amount to forced labour; trade unions remain banned; and there is no non-discriminatory minimum wage.
evidence.source: Human Rights Watch, World Report 2026 (United Arab Emirates)

notes: Filed under the magnitude trigger (+6.2) with recommendation flag-for-review, not upgrade, because the evidence genuinely conflicts: enacted positive conduct by an emirate-level court, reported only by state and state-adjacent sources, set against an independently documented kafala system, union ban and absence of a fair minimum wage. A reviewer may reasonably hold the score at 21.9 pending independent corroboration of the wage-recovery and dispute-resolution figures; that judgement is deliberately left to a human. No band change. Confidence low: delta close to the 5-point threshold and signals conflicting. Evidence gap: no data on domestic workers, who are largely outside the labour-court route, and no Abu Dhabi-specific rights reporting dated inside the window.
